I have been having a difficult time keeping shrimp alive in my tank for more than a few days. I started out with Ghost Shrimp but wasn't too surprised that they died quickly since they are just a cheap feeder variety. I decided to buy some more expensive Red Cherry Shrimp and these too died within a week. Possibly most alarming, I added some pond snails on two different occasions and both times these have also died off. When I test my water everything comes in fairly normal besides being a bit acidic, about 6.5, and hard water. From my research I don't see why these would be so bad as to cause quick death in the shrimp. I even bought a copper testing kit and it came out negative. In the meantime, my fish (Betta, Neon Tetra, and Otos) are doing well. Also doing well are my Malaysian Trumpet Snails which I usually see every morning before the burrow back into the substrate for the day. Any advice for what else I might need to test to get to the bottom of this would be appreciated.

TL;DR: My shrimp are dying even though my numbers on traditional tests are fairly normal/safe levels.

I have an idea that instead of being limited to requiring 100 comments before you can downvote something make it cost comment points. Such as 1 downvote costs 2 or 3 points. You earn your points through getting upvotes. To prevent people from just creating subverses that are used to pad points make upvotes cost 1 point but each day each user gets a set amount of free upvotes like 10 or 25 before the upvotes start costing points.

This prevents people from just going through someone's post history and downvoting everything because they don't like him and at the same time promotes interaction from users to gain more points.
Another thing we can do is in order for a voat to count, it cannot be voted from the users profile. This makes sure that downvoat troll votes do not count.
That's not a bad idea. Downvoting a comment without seeing the context is pretty trollish.
I agree. It's pretty stupid Reddit allows this.
Hmm, I dunno. I do not like the idea of a vote not counting in general. If I press up vote, I want that number to go up. I don't want my vote to be hidden, that leads to shadow-bans and the like.

Other possible improvements:

500 upvotes to create a new sub. It prevents sub squatting, also encourages users to hang around a bit and breath the new air in other subs.

1 000 000 upvotes to remove a mod. Sometimes mods go bad and there is nothing the community can do about it. That was the situation at Reddit and it is the same here. This way a malicious mod can be ousted by the community if 1000 people agree to part with 1000 upvoats each. Of course other people may voat the other way around to keep the mod. It is democratic and civil.

I like these ideas as well. 1 Mil to remove a mod is good, probably 2 Mil to remove the sub creator. But also with the cost to create a sub and the possibility to be removed forcefully do you think the creator then should have the ability to sell the sub for even more points later on? This would encourage people make subs as soon as possible for a possible "profit" later, or to get out with some points if the users don't like you
I'm not really sure about the trade stuff. 1M to remove a mod is not exactly trade, it is more like a blood sacrifice for the greater good. Different things.
